summary.headline: Rust now carries real ML products; the gaps are tracking, tabular parity and mobile.
summary.summary: Rust is a sound choice for inference, retrieval, speech, documents, video and numerical work shipped on one machine: pure-Rust engines exist for LLM and ONNX inference, tokenizing, full-text and vector search, FFT and linear algebra. It is weaker where teams need XGBoost parity, maintained multi-object tracking, a reinforcement-learning trainer, or Rust-native phone inference. Python stays useful for checkpoint conversion and quantization, ONNX export, tokenizer extraction and plotting, but none of that has to sit in your serving path. Treat ONNX Runtime, libtorch, llama.cpp and MKL as accelerators you call, not as Rust work.

jobs.verdict: Quantized LLM inference and OpenAI-compatible serving work: [[mistralrs]] builds pure Rust by default, [[blazr]], [[candle-vllm]] and [[furnace]] serve OpenAI routes, [[tract]] and [[oxionnx]] cover ONNX. All are early releases with thin model coverage.

Hosted-API clients, MCP and schema-constrained output are shipping grade: [[rmcp]] is the official MCP SDK, [[async-openai]] and [[liter-llm]] cover providers, [[rstructor]] enforces schemas. Agent frameworks are early releases that churn.

Single-GPU training and LoRA fine-tuning work with [[burn]], [[candle]] and [[oxidizr]]. [[rumus]] adds FSDP plus tensor and pipeline parallel paths on WebGPU; [[oxidizr]] stops at NCCL data parallelism. No maintained RL trainer exists.

ASR, TTS, VAD, diarization and audio decode all have working crates: [[earshot]] and [[sonora]] are pure Rust, [[parakeet-rs]] and [[transcribe-rs]] route through ONNX Runtime, [[sherpa-onnx]] wraps C. Model and format coverage are the limits.

Tokenizers, embeddings, vector stores and full-text search are covered: [[tantivy]] for BM25, [[qdrant]] for scale, [[tokenizers]] for exact model tokenization. Most embedding and reranking paths still call ONNX Runtime.

Decode and transform are pure Rust in [[kornia-rs]] and [[imageproc]]; [[candle]] runs Stable Diffusion and [[aha]] runs vision and OCR on Candle. Detection and segmentation mostly call ONNX Runtime. No maintained multi-object tracker exists.

[[vidr]] covers decode, encode, container IO and model-on-frame upscaling, with [[containr]] and [[rav1r]] for muxing and AV1. An early release from a lone maintainer, NVIDIA-tested, without VA-API and without H.264 above Baseline.

OCR, PDF extraction and layout are covered: [[ocrs]] and [[franken-ocr]] run in Rust, [[pdf-inspector]] and [[oxidizepdf]] are pure Rust, [[edgeparse]] handles reading order. Broadest format coverage wraps Tesseract, PDFium and ONNX Runtime.

Boosted trees, forests, SVMs, clustering, forecasting and AutoML exist in pure Rust through [[treeboost]], [[linfa]], [[smartcore]] and [[augurs]]. XGBoost and LightGBM parity is unavailable and model-agnostic explanation is thin.

Arrays, dense linear algebra, FFT, sparse matrices, statistics, optimization and ODE solvers are covered in pure Rust by [[ndarray]], [[faer]], [[rustfft]], [[statrs]] and [[differential-equations]]. SciPy breadth is thinner in places; plotting still calls matplotlib.

Tensor math runs on GPU from Rust: [[burn]] ships CUDA, Metal, WebGPU, ROCm and Vulkan, [[candle]] adds CUDA and Metal, [[cubecl]] compiles kernels across vendors, [[numr]] adds NumPy-role tensors. Autodiff works; custom kernels and vendor coverage are uneven.

Model and dataset IO is strong: [[safetensors]], [[gguf]], [[arrow-rs]], [[polars]], [[datafusion]] and [[hf-hub]] are Rust. HDF5 has pure-Rust and wrapped options; legacy PyTorch checkpoint conversion still needs Python.

use_now.use_for: Local LLM inference behind a Rust SDK
use_now.why: Default features build in pure Rust, loads GGUF and multimodal models, and exposes tools, structured output and an MCP client behind a single SDK.
BM25, facets, fast fields and mmap in a library other Rust search engines build on; you write the server layer.

use_now.use_for: Vector search server at production scale
use_now.why: Rust server with sharding, replication, quantization and sparse plus multi-vector search, reached over REST and gRPC.
Official MCP SDK with tools, resources, transports and OAuth; other Rust MCP crates sit on top of it.

use_now.use_for: Call hosted model APIs from Rust
use_now.why: A single async client over many providers with tools, streaming and structured output, so provider churn stays out of your app.
Pure-Rust streaming VAD over short frames, returns a voice score, builds without ONNX Runtime and can run no_std.

use_now.use_for: FFT of any size in pure Rust
use_now.why: SIMD-accelerated transforms of any size including primes; the FFT underneath ndarray and other crates.
Dense linear algebra with decompositions and a high-level API, written in pure Rust so no LAPACK link is needed.
The array container most Rust ML crates share; slicing, views, Zip and optional BLAS keep numeric code portable.
Zero-copy reads and safe writes for model weights; the interchange format Rust trainers and loaders already speak.

use_now.use_for: Fetch models and datasets from the Hub
use_now.why: Async and blocking client for Hub models, datasets and files, native and wasm; keeps download and cache logic out of your code.
Reference BPE, WordPiece and Unigram pipeline with tokenizer.json load and save; matches the main model families.

watch.why: No C or C++ in the build, and real detection models run. Still needs a tokenizer and sampler bolted on, and browser WebGPU is unwired.
Boosted trees and forests with an AutoML mode and SIMD plus GPU backends. No changelog, unstable API and a small team behind it.
Runs the training loop with checkpoints, metrics and resume on a local machine. No FSDP, ZeRO, tensor or pipeline parallelism.

watch.use_for: GPU video decode, encode and upscaling
watch.why: Decode, encode, muxing and upscaling in one workspace with frames kept on the GPU. Early release, NVIDIA-tested, no VA-API, H.264 Baseline only.
Runs document and formula OCR models with Markdown and box output and no FFI. Lone maintainer, CPU only, not a general model runtime.
Static embeddings with int8 quantization and a WASM build, no ONNX Runtime. No training or distillation, and no GPU path.

build_today.goal: Private document Q&A over your own files
build_today.why: [[mistralrs]] generates, [[fastembed-rs]] embeds locally, [[qdrant]] stores and searches, [[swiftide]] wires loaders, chunkers and retrieval into one pipeline.
build_today.watch_out: Both the agent and RAG layers are early releases, and the embedding path pulls in ONNX Runtime.

build_today.goal: Local meeting transcription with speaker labels
build_today.why: [[voxr]] decodes and resamples input, [[earshot]] gates speech, [[parakeet-rs]] transcribes and diarizes on your own hardware.
build_today.watch_out: [[parakeet-rs]] caps speaker count and pass length, and ONNX Runtime limits it to a process-wide environment.

build_today.goal: Search API over your own document corpus
build_today.why: [[tantivy]] scores BM25, [[tokenizers]] matches model tokenization, [[fastembed-rs]] embeds, [[qdrant-client]] queries the store over gRPC.
build_today.watch_out: Hybrid ranking and rerank logic are yours to write; the embedding step needs ONNX Runtime.

build_today.goal: Fine-tune and serve a small model on local hardware
build_today.why: [[oxidizr]] runs the YAML training loop with checkpoints and resume, [[burn]] supplies kernels and autodiff, [[safetensors]] carries weights.
build_today.watch_out: This stack stays on a single machine with NCCL data parallelism; [[oxidizr]] has no FSDP, tensor or pipeline parallelism.

build_today.goal: OCR and PDF extraction for scanned documents
build_today.why: [[pdf-inspector]] separates text from scans, [[ocrs]] reads images, [[edgeparse]] orders columns and tables, [[oxidizepdf]] chunks for retrieval.
build_today.watch_out: OCR models need fetching and release-mode builds; no learned layout unless you add extra models.

holes_filled.hole: Quantized LLM inference plus an OpenAI-compatible server
holes_filled.note: Teams can serve a GGUF model without PyTorch; checkpoint conversion and quantization still use Python first.

holes_filled.hole: ONNX inference with no C or C++ runtime
holes_filled.note: Exported models run in Rust on CPU, Metal, CUDA or WASM; operator coverage and tokenizer or sampler wiring are the cost.

holes_filled.hole: Tokenization that matches the main model families
holes_filled.note: Exact ids without a Python round trip; validate against reference output for the families you depend on.

holes_filled.hole: Full-text and vector search over your own data
holes_filled.note: Both halves of hybrid search exist in Rust; reranking still runs through wrapped ONNX Runtime.

holes_filled.hole: Streaming voice activity detection without a native runtime
holes_filled.note: Gate microphones in pure Rust; learned VAD through ONNX Runtime remains an option when accuracy demands it.

holes_filled.hole: Numerical core: arrays, FFT and dense linear algebra
holes_filled.note: Most SciPy work on a single machine translates; plotting and reference validation stay in Python.

holes_filled.hole: Model and dataset IO for weights and columnar data
holes_filled.note: Read and write the formats trainers and loaders use; legacy PyTorch checkpoints still need conversion tooling.

holes_open.hole: XGBoost and LightGBM parity for tabular models
holes_open.impact: Teams with existing boosted-tree pipelines cannot port them and compare like for like in Rust.
holes_open.workaround: Train with [[treeboost]] or [[perpetual]] and export to XGBoost or ONNX, or keep training in Python.

holes_open.impact: Mobile teams fall back to llama.cpp, whisper.cpp or ONNX Runtime bindings, so the build is not Rust end to end.
holes_open.workaround: [[xybrid]] ships Android and iOS presets but wraps native engines; [[needle-rs]] covers tool-calling models only and leaves NPU work to Cactus.

holes_open.hole: Maintained multi-object tracking across video frames
holes_open.impact: Video analytics teams cannot keep detection-to-track state on a maintained Rust crate; the only tracker row is unmaintained.
holes_open.workaround: [[similari]] has Kalman, SORT, Batch SORT and VisualSORT but is unmaintained; teams write IoU and Hungarian assignment on ndarray or use Python ByteTrack.

holes_open.impact: RL teams get environments but no maintained learner; the older Rust RL crates are unmaintained.
holes_open.workaround: Use [[bevy-rl]] for environments and write the learner on [[burn]] or [[candle]], or keep training in Python.

holes_open.hole: VA-API and H.264 High profile in Rust video
holes_open.impact: Linux teams without NVIDIA cannot decode or encode common camera and screen streams through a Rust path.
holes_open.workaround: [[vidr]] covers NVDEC, NVENC and Vulkan Video plus Baseline H.264 and AV1 on CPU; otherwise transcode with FFmpeg or a Python pipeline.

charts.takeaway: Many projects either contain some native code or wrap a native engine, so pure-Rust implementations are not the norm.
GPU support is frequently unspecified and fragmented across backends, with CUDA the most commonly declared option.
Many projects have shipped recently, but a substantial tail has gone without a release for a long time.
